problem_summary.F-13_cap_overshoot: extractor.costing.record_request_cost priced the actual usage, ADDED it to state.total_cost_usd, appended the ledger entry, and only THEN compared total_cost_usd > max_cost_usd to decide whether to abort. A single call whose own cost exceeded the cap was fully committed to the running total and the durable ledger before the breach was even noticed -- the exact 'record now, notice later' overshoot A2-7 named. Separately, cost_cap_mode was declared on every cost profile ('preventive') and threaded onto RunnerConfig, but no code anywhere branched on its value -- decorative. make_projected_cost_check (extractor/costing.py) was reported dead in v5; verified TRUE (zero callers outside its own module/tests) -- it is a pre-dispatch projected-cost helper for a DIFFERENT mechanism (E2 preview/preventive path) than what E3's post-response accounting needs, so it is not the fix vehicle for F-13 and was left untouched.
problem_summary.F-15_non_atomic_ledger: _write_spend_ledger_snapshot delegated to CostingDeps.write_json, wired to run_extraction_v5.write_json, which does path.write_text(full_json) directly -- a full in-place rewrite of the money log on every single cost event, with no crash-safety: a kill/crash mid-write (or mid-flush-to-disk) truncates or corrupts SPEND_LEDGER.json, the only durable record of what was actually spent.
problem_summary.F-38_temperature: Sampling temperature was hardcoded 0.1 at three independent sites (run_extraction_v5.build_chat_payload's resolve_temperature call; run_extraction_v5._build_gemini_config_for_model, confirmed dead/unreachable -- zero callers; llm_runtime.call_llm's Gemini native-SDK branch, reachable) with no CLI/env/profile control. Only build_chat_payload's resolve_temperature() honored the gpt-5 omission rule (OpenAI gpt-5* models reject the temperature parameter outright); the other hardcode sites didn't consult it at all (latent asymmetry, non-issue today since llm_runtime's Gemini branch is gemini-only and never subject to the openai-only carve-out).

design_summary.F13_fix: record_request_cost now computes projected_total_cost_usd = current_total + this_call's_actual_cost BEFORE any mutation, and (for cost_cap_mode != 'post_hoc', i.e. the default 'preventive' every shipped profile declares) refuses the call when the projection would exceed max_cost_usd: cost_abort_triggered is set, the ledger snapshot is written reflecting the (unchanged) total and the abort, and the function returns WITHOUT incrementing total_cost_usd or appending a ledger entry for the breaching call. The post-append check (`if total_cost_usd > max_cost_usd`) is now scoped to cost_cap_mode == 'post_hoc' only -- an explicit, opt-in-only legacy path (no shipped cost profile sets it) that reproduces the pre-fix commit-then-compare behavior verbatim, so the field is no longer decorative: it selects between two REAL, distinct, tested code paths. Fail-closed: any cost_cap_mode value other than 'preventive'/'post_hoc' (including missing/None) resolves to 'preventive' at initialize_spend_tracker time.
design_summary.F13_make_projected_cost_check_dispositio: Left in place, unmodified. It is a legitimate helper for a pre-dispatch projected-cost check (given a candidate rate + hypothetical usage, before any call is made) -- architecturally the E2/preview-side mechanism, not E3's post-response accounting mechanism this packet fixes. Confirmed dead in v5 (grep across the service: only definition + its own 2 unit tests in test_spend_ledger_optimizers.py reference it; run_extraction_v5.py's actual shipped preventive path is the separate _check_projected_cost_limit). Removing or wiring it was NOT required by F-13 and would have been unrelated scope expansion on a money-critical packet; noted here as explicitly verified rather than assumed.
design_summary.F15_fix: New write_json_atomic() in run_extraction_v5.py: serializes the (same sanitization as write_json, factored into a shared _sanitized_json_payload_for_path helper) payload to a temp file created via tempfile.mkstemp() in the SAME directory as the target (required for os.replace to be atomic on the same filesystem), fsyncs it, then os.replace()s it into the target path. CostingDeps.write_json (the only thing _write_spend_ledger_snapshot calls) is now bound to write_json_atomic instead of the plain write_json -- so every spend-ledger snapshot write goes through the durable path. Every other write_json caller in the service (partition artifacts, telemetry, manifests, etc.) is UNCHANGED -- this is scoped narrowly to the money log per the packet's mandate, not a blanket rewrite of the JSON I/O layer.
design_summary.F38_fix: New RunnerConfig.llm_temperature: float = 0.1 field, new --llm-temperature argparse flag (extractor/cli_args.py, range-validated 0.0-2.0 at both the click layer (src/dopemux/cli.py's `dopemux rte run` wrapper, click.FloatRange) and v5's own argparse layer (extractor/cli_args.py registers the flag; run_extraction_v5.main() validates via the new pure _llm_temperature_out_of_range() helper and parser.error()s on violation)). build_chat_payload gained a default_temperature: float = 0.1 parameter that is passed to resolve_temperature() as the default (resolve_temperature remains the SINGLE choke point for the gpt-5 omission rule -- untouched). The one reachable v5 call site (execute_step_for_partitions -> build_chat_payload) now passes default_temperature=cfg.llm_temperature. llm_runtime.call_llm forwards default_temperature=getattr(cfg, 'llm_temperature', 0.1) into its deps.build_chat_payload call (closing that path too) and its own Gemini native-SDK config dict now reads getattr(cfg, 'llm_temperature', 0.1) instead of a bare 0.1 literal (gemini is never subject to the gpt-5 carve-out, so no omission logic was needed there). _build_gemini_config_for_model (confirmed dead, zero callers) was left untouched -- editing dead code was assessed as unnecessary scope on a money-critical packet.
design_summary.src_dopemux_cli_py_justification: Touched under the dispatch instruction's explicit carve-out ('plus src/dopemux/cli.py ONLY if the flag definition requires it'). The canonical operator entrypoint per F-42/CONSOLIDATED-FINDINGS is `dopemux rte run`, which builds a v5 argv list explicitly (one click.option + one forwarding line per flag, mirroring the existing --max-cost-usd pattern at cli.py:5185-5189/5325-5326) -- without this, --llm-temperature would only be reachable via direct `python run_extraction_v5.py` invocation, not the documented operator path.
design_summary.extractor_cli_args_py_boundary_note: This file is NOT in the packet's literal file-boundary list (which predates the R1-002 seam extraction that moved run_extraction_v5.py's argparse definitions -- including the analogous --max-cost-usd -- into extractor/cli_args.py). run_extraction_v5.py's own build_parser() is now a thin wrapper delegating to extractor.cli_args.build_parser(context). Registering a new argparse flag is structurally impossible without touching this file post-R1-002; treated as covered by the same 'files moved in R2-001[/R1-002]' allowance the dispatch prompt gave for line numbers, applied to the one file whose absence from the stale boundary list would make the third required outcome unimplementable. Flagged explicitly here rather than silently done.

files_not_touched: lib/spend_ledger.py -- in the packet's allowed boundary but not edited. E2's preview/preventive path already runs an unconditional, genuine pre-dispatch check (_check_projected_cost_limit in run_extraction_v5.py) independent of cost_cap_mode; F-13 is specifically an E3 (extractor.costing.record_request_cost) defect. Wiring cost_cap_mode into E2 as well was out of the named defect's scope and risked destabilizing the already-unified E2/E3 parity R2-001 just proved (test_pricing_authority_unification.py).
config/pricing.yaml, promptsets/** -- excluded per explicit file-boundary instruction.
extractor/costing.py's make_projected_cost_check -- verified dead, left unmodified (see design_summary.F13_make_projected_cost_check_disposition).
run_extraction_v5.py's _build_gemini_config_for_model -- verified dead (zero callers), left unmodified rather than editing unreachable code.
cost_cap_mode_disposition: WIRED (not removed). Rationale: every one of the 11 shipped cost profiles already declares cost_cap_mode: "preventive" and the field already flows onto RunnerConfig -- removing it would have required touching config declarations across all 11 profiles for no behavioral gain, whereas wiring it gives the field real, tested, opposite-behavior semantics (preventive = pre-check before commit, the new default-matching fix; post_hoc = the exact pre-fix commit-then-compare behavior, opt-in only, zero shipped profiles use it) with a fail-closed fallback (any other/missing value -> preventive). This closes the 'decorative field' half of F-13 with the minimal change: one new branch in record_request_cost keyed off a field that was already being computed and passed everywhere, no profile-file edits needed.
